facts.fact: 早餐自助餐摆在台面上（香肠／蛋／粗玉米粉）
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia had set out a breakfast buffet on the counter, complete with sausage, eggs, and grits

facts.fact: 她端了盘子，跟 Virginia 坐在与厨房相连的明亮通风房间里
facts.anchor: I grabbed a plate and joined her in a light-filled, breezy room connected to the kitchen

facts.fact: Virginia 正在给一盆紫色非洲堇浇水
facts.anchor: where she was watering a purple African violet

facts.fact: 暖房既属于 Greer House 又不属于它
facts.anchor: The conservatory was part of Greer House, yet also apart from it

facts.fact: 没有墙，由锻铁与玻璃窗构成围合
facts.anchor: the enclosure was framed by a combination of intricate wrought iron and glass windows

facts.fact: 地面是黑白格瓷砖
facts.anchor: its floor was black-and-white checkered tile

facts.fact: 暖房是 Virginia 的母亲为怕佛罗里达气候的植物建的
facts.anchor: it was built by her mother for plants too sensitive for Florida’s weather

facts.fact: 她伤心地补一句：在里面也好不了多少，并摸另一株枯萎的植物
facts.anchor: “Though they barely do better in here,” she added sadly, fingering another wilting plant

facts.fact: 她说了一句「这该死的房子」
facts.anchor: “This damn house.”

facts.fact: 叙述者坐进黑白条纹坐垫的藤椅，喝冰茶、心不在焉地欣赏红色积水凤梨
facts.anchor: Settling into a rattan chair with a black-and-white-striped seat cushion

facts.fact: Virginia 细数下午要进城散步的安排
facts.anchor: listened to Aunt Virginia detail the stroll we’d take downtown that afternoon

facts.fact: 她本该问 Gazzie 不肯答的那些问题（农场与衣橱上的字）
facts.anchor: I should have asked her the questions Gazzie wouldn’t answer about the farm and the ominous words in Mama’s closet

facts.fact: 她不想让 Gazzie 听见、再次把她冻在外面
facts.anchor: I didn’t want Gazzie to overhear and freeze me out again

facts.fact: 她需要找到能多与她相处的办法
facts.anchor: I needed to find a way to spend more time with her

facts.fact: 问题一成形答案就咔哒落位
facts.anchor: The answer clicked as soon as the question formed

facts.fact: 她脱口而出想在农场干活
facts.anchor: “I’d like to work at the farm while I’m here,” I blurted out

facts.fact: Virginia 扬眉、唇边一丝笑
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia raised her eyebrows, the hint of a smile on her lips

facts.fact: 她谎称今早 Gazzie 跟她多讲了农场，她想看看真实的样子
facts.anchor: “Gazzie told me more about it this morning, and I want to see what it’s like. For real.

facts.fact: 她底气不足地补：这是她的遗产
facts.anchor: At Aunt Virginia’s continued silence, I added, less certainly, “Since it’s my heritage and all.”

facts.fact: Virginia 把洒水壶放在格砖地上、坐进旁边的椅子、急切前倾
facts.anchor: She set her watering can on the checkered floor and slid into the chair beside mine, leaning forward eagerly

facts.fact: 她说很高兴听她这么说
facts.anchor: “I’m so glad to hear you say that.”

facts.fact: 叙述者点明：她原来一直在偷偷盼着这句
facts.anchor: Apparently, she’d been secretly hoping for this

facts.fact: 她问 Gazzie 会不会允许
facts.anchor: “Do you think she’ll let me?”

facts.fact: Virginia 打包票：她会允许，别担心
facts.anchor: “Oh, she’ll let you. Don’t you worry.”

facts.fact: 在叙述者眉眼大开时 Virginia 清了清嗓子说要坦白一件事
facts.anchor: As I beamed, Aunt Virginia cleared her throat. “But I do want to confess something.”

facts.fact: 叙述者皮肤因期待而发麻
facts.anchor: My skin prickled with anticipation

facts.fact: Virginia 承认自己一直没有完全坦白
facts.anchor: “I haven’t been entirely honest with you,”

facts.fact: 她说话时目光跟着一只从橡树俯冲下来的 mockingbird
facts.anchor: eyes tracking a mockingbird as it swooped down from the oak tree outside

facts.fact: 她解释自己一直紧张、怕这通折腾把她吓跑
facts.anchor: Worried this whole hullabaloo might scare you off.

facts.fact: 叙述者想到 Gazzie 提过的农场麻烦，猜比她暗示的严重
facts.anchor: My mind flitted to the farm problems Gazzie had mentioned. They must be more serious than she’d implied

facts.fact: 坦白内容第一条：那封信是我写给你母亲的
facts.anchor: “First off,” she said, “I wrote that letter to your mother.”

facts.fact: 叙述者没想到，并问是 Gazzie 签的字吗
facts.anchor: I hadn’t expected that. “And Gazzie signed it?”

facts.fact: Virginia：同住一辈子就把一个人的签名认得很熟了
facts.anchor: “After a life in the same house, you get to know a person’s signature pretty well.”

facts.fact: 叙述者归纳：她伪造了签名、撒了谎
facts.anchor: She’d forged it. Lied.

facts.fact: 所以信是让妈妈发邮件给 Virginia 而非 Gazzie
facts.anchor: That’s why the letter had asked Mama to email Aunt Virginia, not Gazzie

facts.fact: 所以信里说 Gazzie 不看邮件也不接电话
facts.anchor: Why it had claimed Gazzie didn’t check her email or answer phone calls

facts.fact: Virginia 想在妈妈真正与 Greer 家重逢前先把谎铺好
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia had wanted to get ahead of the lie before Mama actually reunited with the Greers.

facts.fact: 愤怒与困惑同时她承认自己发邮件时也撒过谎
facts.anchor: Anger and confusion twisted inside me, even as part of me acknowledged I’d lied when I emailed her

facts.fact: 她那封邮件说的是妈妈本意要让她们相见
facts.anchor: saying Mama had intended for us to meet

facts.fact: 但她仍是被 Virginia 操纵着来相见的
facts.anchor: Still—she’d manipulated me into meeting her.

facts.fact: 她的目光落在积水凤梨上、手指发痒想抓花盆
facts.anchor: My eyes fell on the bromeliad, my fingers itching to grab the pot

facts.fact: 想象把盆砸向 Virginia 的头、陶土在她颧骨上碎成千片
facts.anchor: I could hurl it at Aunt Virginia’s head, watch the terracotta shatter into a thousand sharp pieces against her cheekbone

facts.fact: 她僵住、眨掉那个画面，自问怎么了
facts.anchor: I froze, blinked away the image. What was wrong with me?

facts.fact: Virginia 没注意到，因坦白难为情而把脸别开
facts.anchor: She didn’t notice. Embarrassed by her confession, she’d looked away.

facts.fact: Virginia 说知道 Gazzie 的签名能引起 Caroline 注意、Gazzie 也想见她
facts.anchor: I knew Gazzie’s signature would get Caroline’s attention and that Gazzie would love to see her if I could just get her here.

facts.fact: Virginia 说没看出这有什么伤害、希望别太生她的气
facts.anchor: I didn’t see the harm in it, and I hope you aren’t too mad at me, honey.

facts.fact: 叙述者答「没事」，愤怒已被羞耻压过
facts.anchor: “It’s okay,” I replied, anger already overcome by shame.

facts.fact: 她把手覆在 Virginia 手上握住，急着安慰她
facts.anchor: I placed my hand on hers and squeezed it, eager to console her.

facts.fact: 她自陈此举是为了证明自己是善良宽容的人
facts.anchor: To prove I was a kind, forgiving person.

facts.fact: Virginia 把手抽回、把辫子翻到肩上、开始摩挲缎带
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia pulled her hand out from under mine, flipped her braid over her shoulder, and began to stroke the ribbon

facts.fact: 话头转向：Gazzie 今年要在至日派对上做点不一样的
facts.anchor: “The thing is, Gazzie wants to do something different at the solstice party this year.”

facts.fact: 每年夏至庆祝生意创立
facts.anchor: Every summer solstice, we celebrate the business’s founding.

facts.fact: 那是 Ida 的纪念日（被截断）
facts.anchor: It’s the anniversary of Ida—

facts.fact: 叙述者接完：射杀 Ironheart，并说这是 Gazzie 告诉她的
facts.anchor: “Shooting Ironheart,” I finished, showing off my new knowledge. “Gazzie told me.”

facts.fact: 那是个大日子
facts.anchor: “It’s a real big time.

facts.fact: 派对当晚房子一带的天气总是配合
facts.anchor: the weather always behaves around the house the evening of

facts.fact: 弦乐四重奏演奏 Jimmy Buffett、小猪香肠、鱼子酱、有时整猪烤肉、总是很多酒
facts.anchor: We have a string quartet playing Jimmy Buffett, pigs in blankets, caviar, sometimes a hog roast, always a lot of booze.

facts.fact: 她每年发誓不再喝却一有客人就灌 hurricanes
facts.anchor: Every year I swear I’ll never drink again, yet I find myself downing hurricanes soon as the first guest arrives.

facts.fact: 她想象自己穿碎花连衣裙配高跟鞋、手拿 margarita
facts.anchor: me in a flowery sundress and matching heels, margarita in hand

facts.fact: 想象 Gazzie 把她介绍给自己的所有朋友
facts.anchor: Gazzie introducing me to all her friends

facts.fact: 她问今年有什么不一样
facts.anchor: “What’s different about this year?” I asked.

facts.fact: Virginia：你祖母不是要退休——她永远不会退休，老顽固——但她要公开指定继承人
facts.anchor: Your grandmother isn’t going to retire—she’ll never retire, the old donkey—but she wants to name an heir. Publicly.

facts.fact: Virginia 提醒她第一次一起吃饭时提过这事
facts.anchor: She mentioned it during our first dinner together, remember?

facts.fact: Virginia 说她自己心里有别人选
facts.anchor: Well, I have someone different in mind.

facts.fact: 叙述者立刻表态支持，尽管没听懂重点
facts.anchor: “You have my support,” I said earnestly, though I didn’t understand the point.

facts.fact: 她估计 Virginia 不少于七十岁
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia couldn’t be younger than seventy.

facts.fact: 她算出就算接掌也最多在 Gazzie 死后管几年
facts.anchor: She’d be in charge for, at most, a few years after Gazzie’s death.

facts.fact: 她认为 Gazzie 已经铁了心选定了谁
facts.anchor: Plus, Gazzie seemed set on whomever she’d already picked.

facts.fact: Virginia 大笑：主啊别、你拿枪逼我接我都不接
facts.anchor: “Lord, no, Dartrine. You couldn’t force me to take over at gunpoint.”

facts.fact: 她一哆嗦，辫子咚地砸在胸前
facts.anchor: She shuddered, her braid falling to her chest with a solid thump.

facts.fact: 这不是关于我
facts.anchor: “This isn’t about me.

facts.fact: 自 1800 年代末创立起这就是家族生意
facts.anchor: ours is a family business and has been since its founding in the late 1800s

facts.fact: 农场与宅子经三代 Greer 女性传下
facts.anchor: The farm and house have passed down through three generations of Greer women

facts.fact: 她无法想象它脱离她们的掌控
facts.anchor: I can’t imagine it falling out of our control.”

facts.fact: 叙述者忽然懂了，问是不是想让她来接
facts.anchor: Suddenly, I understood. “You’re saying you want me to—

facts.fact: Virginia：本指望她母亲接，现在轮到你
facts.anchor: “I’d hoped your mother might take over. But now, it’s up to you.”

facts.fact: 两只松鼠在外面的露台上赛跑
facts.anchor: Two squirrels raced across the patio outside.

facts.fact: Virginia 目送它们；叙述者又困惑又兴奋
facts.anchor: Aunt Virginia gazed after them while I processed her words, bewildered but excited.

facts.fact: 她曾幻想从 HR 经理一路升到总监、日后搬去亚特兰大／夏洛特／华盛顿特区的营利公司
facts.anchor: I’d daydreamed about working my way up from HR manager to director, one day moving to a for-profit business in Atlanta or Charlotte or DC.

facts.fact: 但作为已有生意的主人与 Greer 财富的继承人，她不必为安全感把身体耗干
facts.anchor: as the owner of an established business and heir to the Greers’ wealth, I wouldn’t have to run my poorly functioning body into the ground for security

facts.fact: 她问那已经选定的继承人怎么办
facts.anchor: “But what about the heir she’s already chosen?” I asked.

facts.fact: Virginia 坚决地说外人继承她受不了、连 Harrison 也不行
facts.anchor: “An outsider inheriting doesn’t sit right with me,” Aunt Virginia said resolutely, straightening in the chair. “Not even Harrison.”

facts.fact: 这个名字像钢墙一样撞上来
facts.anchor: His name hit me like a steel wall.

facts.fact: 于是他就是 Gazzie 的既定继承人
facts.anchor: So he was Gazzie’s heir apparent.

facts.fact: 难怪第一天他在宅子里逗留
facts.anchor: No wonder he’d lingered at the house that first day.

facts.fact: 难怪 Gazzie 靠他管理农场里那桩不知所谓的事
facts.anchor: No wonder Gazzie relied on him to manage whatever the hell was going on at the farm

facts.fact: 难怪他一见面就讨厌她；他和 Gazzie 一样以为她为遗产而来
facts.anchor: he, like Gazzie, had assumed I’d come to Florida for the inheritance.

facts.fact: 在他眼里她是个闯入者
facts.anchor: To him, I was an interloper.

facts.fact: 她承认他并不全错、心往下沉
facts.anchor: And he wasn’t entirely wrong, I thought, stomach sinking.

facts.fact: Virginia 让她在农场尽力了解这门生意
facts.anchor: do your best to get to know the business.

facts.fact: 她一有能力 Gazzie 就会改主意
facts.anchor: She’ll change her mind once she sees you’re capable.”

facts.fact: 叙述者总结：要她在至日前学完整门生意来赢过 Gazzie
facts.anchor: “You want me to learn the entire business before solstice. To win over Gazzie.”

facts.fact: Virginia：只要让 Gazzie 看到你愿意学；尽管她有抵触，她是——（找词）家庭观念重的
facts.anchor: Just show Gazzie you’re willing to learn. Despite her resistance, she’s—” Aunt Virginia searched for the right word. “Family oriented.

facts.fact: 这是她的机会：永久职位、永久生活、一个（有朝一日）爱她的家
facts.anchor: This was my chance. A permanent position, a permanent life, a family that loved me—or would love me one day, I hoped.

facts.fact: 她说她干了，气喘吁吁
facts.anchor: “I’m in,” I said breathlessly.

facts.fact: Virginia：好，你明天开始
facts.anchor: “Good,” she replied. “You’ll start tomorrow.”

relations: Virginia 与叙述者：姑侄／姨妈（本章以 Aunt Virginia 相称，且她叫叙述者 honey）
Caroline＝Mama 的名字，本章在 Virginia 口中第一次出现
I knew Gazzie’s signature would get Caroline’s attention
Dartrine＝叙述者的全名，本章由 Virginia 叫出
Harrison：Virginia 称他是「外人」，叙述者推定他是 Gazzie 的既定继承人
Ironheart：叙述者用 ch05／ch08 得来的知识替 Virginia 接话
Solstice 派对：庆祝生意创立、Ida 射杀 Ironheart 的周年
